subproblem.title: Area formula on an embedded C¹ submanifold for a C¹ map that is injective with injective derivative (Simon Ch. 2, 4.11–4.13, as used in 5.1–5.2)
subproblem.statement: Area formula on an embedded C¹ submanifold. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; M ⊆ ℝ^P; a Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P; a map Φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Hypotheses: M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M); E is Borel (MeasurableSet E) and E ⊆ M; Φ is C¹ on ℝ^P; Φ is injective on E; the derivative DΦ(x) = fderiv ℝ Φ x is injective for every x ∈ E. Notation: for x ∈ ℝ^P let T_x := span(tangentSpace M x) (a linear subspace, with the inner product of ℝ^P) and ι_x : T_x → ℝ^P the inclusion; J^MΦ(x) := √det((DΦ(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ(x)∘ι_x)), where * is the adjoint for the inner products of T_x and ℝ^P and det is the determinant of the endomorphism (DΦ(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ(x)∘ι_x) of T_x. Conclusion: H^m(Φ(E)) = ∫_E J^MΦ dH^m as an equality in [0, ∞], where H^m = μHE[m] and the integrand is read through ENNReal.ofReal (a lower Lebesgue integral ∫⁻ over E).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 4.11–4.13 (area formula on a submanifold through local representations and the Jacobian factorization J_{f∘ψ} = J_ψ·J^M_f of 4.11), as used in Ch. 2, 5.1–5.2 (H^n(φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^n) and in step (0c) of the supplied proof of the parent. The Euclidean area formula used below is the kernel-checked SimonGMT theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Simon (3.2) for a map that is injective with injective derivative on a measurable set). Sibling lemmas: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv) and locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed).

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]. For a finite-dimensional real inner product space S and a linear map L : S → ℝ^P put J(L) := √det(L*L). The endomorphism L*L of S is positive semidefinite, so det(L*L) ≥ 0, and for every orthonormal basis s_1, …, s_k of S, det(L*L) = det(Ls_i·Ls_j)_{i,j} (a Gram determinant). J(L) is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet L (normDet_sq). With this notation J^MΦ(x) = J(DΦ(x)∘ι_x).

1. (Jacobian factorization, Simon 4.11.) Let A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be linear and injective with range R, and B : ℝ^P → ℝ^P linear. Then J(B∘A) = J(A)·J(B∘ι_R), ι_R : R → ℝ^P the inclusion.
 Proof. Write A = ι_R∘S with S : ℝ^m → R a linear isomorphism. Then A*A = S*S and (BA)*(BA) = S*(Bι_R)*(Bι_R)S. Computing determinants in orthonormal bases of ℝ^m and of R, det(S*CS) = det(S)²·det(C) for every endomorphism C of R. Hence det((BA)*(BA)) = det(S)²·det((Bι_R)*(Bι_R)) = det(A*A)·det((Bι_R)*(Bι_R)); take square roots. (This is also SimonGMT areaJacobian_comp_eq_parametrization_mul_tangential and Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp.)

2. (Countable chart cover.) For each y ∈ M fix a chart (V_y, W_y, ψ_y) as in IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M: V_y ⊆ ℝ^m and W_y ⊆ ℝ^P open, y ∈ W_y, ψ_y C¹ and injective on V_y, ψ_y(V_y) = W_y ∩ M, V_y ∩ ψ_y^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W_y, and Dψ_y(v) injective for v ∈ V_y. By chart_tangent_space, tangentSpace M (ψ_y(v)) = range Dψ_y(v) for v ∈ V_y; this is an m-dimensional linear subspace, so T_{ψ_y(v)} = range Dψ_y(v). Since ℝ^P is second countable, the open cover {W_y}_{y∈M} of M has a countable subcover {W_k}_{k≥1}; let (V_k, W_k, ψ_k) be the corresponding charts. Put E_k := (E ∩ W_k) ∖ (W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_{k−1}). The E_k are Borel, pairwise disjoint, and ⋃_k E_k = E, because E ⊆ M ⊆ ⋃_k W_k.

3. (Each chart is a homeomorphism onto W_k ∩ M.) ψ_k is continuous and injective on V_k with image W_k ∩ M. If z_j ∈ V_k and ψ_k(z_j) → ψ_k(z) with z ∈ V_k, then K := {ψ_k(z_j) : j} ∪ {ψ_k(z)} is a compact subset of W_k, so all z_j lie in the compact set V_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(K); every cluster point z' ∈ V_k of (z_j) satisfies ψ_k(z') = ψ_k(z), hence z' = z; so z_j → z. Thus ψ_k^{-1} : W_k ∩ M → V_k is continuous.

4. (Pieces in coordinates.) Let F_k := V_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(E_k), a Borel subset of ℝ^m (ψ_k is continuous on the open set V_k). Since E_k ⊆ W_k ∩ M = ψ_k(V_k) and ψ_k is injective on V_k, ψ_k(F_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(B)) = E_k ∩ B for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P.

5. (Euclidean area formula.) Let f be ψ_k or Φ∘ψ_k, and let F ⊆ F_k be Borel. At every v ∈ F (an interior point of V_k), f is differentiable with derivative Dψ_k(v), respectively DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v) (chain rule); both are injective, since Dψ_k(v) is injective and DΦ(ψ_k(v)) is injective (ψ_k(v) ∈ E). f is injective on F (ψ_k is injective on V_k, and Φ is injective on E ⊇ ψ_k(F)). By injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (with finrank ℝ^m = m; on ℝ^m the measure μHE[m] is Lebesgue measure L^m),
 (5.1) H^m(ψ_k(F)) = ∫_F J(Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v),
 (5.2) H^m(Φ(ψ_k(F))) = ∫_F J(DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v).

6. (Change of variables on E_k.) For every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫_{E_k} g dH^m = ∫_{F_k} g(ψ_k(v))·J(Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v). For g = 1_B (B Borel) this is (5.1) with F := F_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(B), by step 4. Both sides are additive and positively homogeneous in g, so the identity holds for nonnegative simple Borel functions, and by monotone convergence for every Borel g ≥ 0.

7. (J^MΦ is Borel on M.) For v ∈ V_k, step 1 with A := Dψ_k(v) (whose range is T_{ψ_k(v)}, step 2) and B := DΦ(ψ_k(v)) gives
 (7.1) J(DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v)) = J(Dψ_k(v))·J^MΦ(ψ_k(v)), with J(Dψ_k(v)) > 0.
 The maps v ↦ J(Dψ_k(v)) and v ↦ J(DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v)) are continuous on V_k (Dψ_k and DΦ are continuous, and Gram determinants are polynomials in inner products). By (7.1), v ↦ J^MΦ(ψ_k(v)) is continuous on V_k, so by step 3 J^MΦ is continuous on the relatively open set W_k ∩ M. As the W_k cover M, the restriction of J^MΦ to M is continuous. M is Borel (locally_closed, part (a)), hence g := 1_M·J^MΦ is a Borel function on ℝ^P, and g = J^MΦ on E.

8. (Area formula on E_k.) By (5.2) with F := F_k, by (7.1), and by step 6 applied to g:
 H^m(Φ(E_k)) = ∫_{F_k} J^MΦ(ψ_k(v))·J(Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v) = ∫_{E_k} J^MΦ dH^m.

9. (Summation.) Each Φ(E_k) is Borel, because Φ is continuous and injective on the Borel set E_k (Lusin–Souslin; Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). The sets Φ(E_k) are pairwise disjoint because Φ is injective on E. Hence
 H^m(Φ(E)) = Σ_k H^m(Φ(E_k)) = Σ_k ∫_{E_k} J^MΦ dH^m = ∫_E J^MΦ dH^m,
 the last equality by countable additivity of E' ↦ ∫_{E'} g dH^m over the disjoint Borel sets E_k. Since J^MΦ ≥ 0, the right side is ∫⁻_E ENNReal.ofReal(J^MΦ) dH^m, and J^MΦ(x) is exactly √det((DΦ(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ(x)∘ι_x)) with T_x = span(tangentSpace M x) (= tangentSpace M x for x ∈ M). This is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Jacobian factorization J(B∘A) = J(A)·J(B restricted to range A) for injective A (Simon 4.11).
Cover M by countably many charts and split E into disjoint Borel pieces E_k = ψ_k(F_k) inside chart domains.
Apply SimonGMT injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative to ψ_k and to Φ∘ψ_k on F_k, and derive ∫_{E_k} g dH^m = ∫_{F_k} g∘ψ_k·J(Dψ_k) for Borel g ≥ 0.
J^MΦ is continuous on M (chart coordinates), so H^m(Φ(E_k)) = ∫_{E_k} J^MΦ dH^m.
Sum over k: the Φ(E_k) are Borel (Lusin–Souslin) and pairwise disjoint, giving H^m(Φ(E)) = ∫_E J^MΦ dH^m.

subproblem.title: A C¹ hypercone of A₀ whose unit normal has zero tangential derivative is a punctured m-plane (parent step 10)
subproblem.statement: Flat cones are planes. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P; ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Hypotheses: m ≥ 2; dim A₀ = m + 1; M ≠ ∅; M ⊆ A₀; 0 ∉ M; M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M); closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0}; tx ∈ M for every x ∈ M and t > 0; ν is differentiable at every x ∈ M; for every x ∈ M, ν(x) ∈ A₀, |ν(x)| = 1 and ν(x)·v = 0 for every v ∈ tangentSpace M x; and Dν(x)v = 0 (fderiv ℝ ν x v = 0) for every x ∈ M and v ∈ tangentSpace M x. Conclusion: there is a linear subspace H₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with dim H₀ = m (Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m) and M = H₀ ∖ {0}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 10 of the supplied proof of the parent (step B9 of its own parent): |A| ≡ 0 makes the unit normal locally constant, each connected component of the cone M is a punctured hyperplane of A₀ through 0, and since m ≥ 2 all components coincide. Sibling lemma: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv).

Notation. T_x := tangentSpace M x. For a chart (V, W, ψ) of M (as in IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M) and v ∈ V, chart_tangent_space gives T_{ψ(v)} = range Dψ(v). ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto the relatively open set W ∩ M (continuous and injective, and proper: if ψ(z_j) → ψ(z), all z_j lie in the compact preimage of {ψ(z_j)} ∪ {ψ(z)} and every cluster point equals z); hence ψ maps open subsets of V onto relatively open subsets of M.

1. (ν is locally constant on M.) Let x ∈ M, (V, W, ψ) a chart at x and B ⊆ V an open ball around ψ^{-1}(x). For v ∈ B and a ∈ ℝ^m, ν∘ψ is differentiable at v (ψ is differentiable at the interior point v, ν at ψ(v) ∈ M) with D(ν∘ψ)(v)a = Dν(ψ(v))(Dψ(v)a) = 0, because Dψ(v)a ∈ T_{ψ(v)}. So ν∘ψ has zero derivative on the convex set B and is constant there (mean value theorem). ψ(B) is a relatively open neighbourhood of x in M, and it is connected. Hence ν is locally constant on M.

2. (Components.) M is locally connected (each point has the connected relatively open neighbourhoods ψ(B)), so its connected components are open and closed in M. Let M_c be a component. ν is locally constant on the connected set M_c, hence constant there: ν ≡ ν_c on M_c, with ν_c ∈ A₀ and |ν_c| = 1.

3. (M_c lies in a hyperplane of A₀ through 0.) Let f(z) := ν_c·z. For z ∈ M_c with chart ψ and ball B as in step 1, ψ(B) is connected and meets M_c, so ψ(B) ⊆ M_c; for v ∈ B and a ∈ ℝ^m, D(f∘ψ)(v)a = ν_c·Dψ(v)a = ν(ψ(v))·Dψ(v)a = 0 (normality and Dψ(v)a ∈ T_{ψ(v)}). So f is locally constant on M_c, hence constant: f ≡ c_c on M_c. For z ∈ M_c the ray {tz : t > 0} lies in M (cone property), is connected and contains z, so it lies in M_c; thus c_c = f(tz) = t·f(z) = t·c_c for every t > 0, and c_c = 0. Hence M_c ⊆ H_c := A₀ ∩ ν_c^⊥, a linear subspace of dimension m (ν_c is a nonzero vector of the (m+1)-dimensional A₀).

4. (M_c is open in H_c.) Let z ∈ M_c, with ψ and B as in step 3, so ψ(B) ⊆ M_c ⊆ H_c. As ψ takes values in the closed subspace H_c on B, Dψ(v) maps ℝ^m into H_c for v ∈ B; it is injective and dim H_c = m, so Dψ(v) : ℝ^m → H_c is an isomorphism. By the inverse function theorem (applied to ψ|_B as a C¹ map into H_c ≅ ℝ^m), ψ|_B is an open map into H_c, so ψ(B) is an open subset of H_c containing z. Hence M_c is open in H_c.

5. (M_c is closed in H_c ∖ {0}.) closure(M_c) ⊆ closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0}, and closure(M_c) ∩ M = M_c because M_c is closed in M. Hence closure(M_c) ∖ {0} ⊆ M_c, i.e. M_c is closed in ℝ^P ∖ {0}, and therefore closed in H_c ∖ {0}. Also M_c ⊆ H_c ∖ {0} because 0 ∉ M.

6. (M_c = H_c ∖ {0}.) H_c ∖ {0} is connected because dim H_c = m ≥ 2 (a real vector space of dimension ≥ 2 minus a point is path-connected). M_c is nonempty, open (step 4) and closed (step 5) in H_c ∖ {0}, so M_c = H_c ∖ {0}.

7. (All components give the same plane.) Let M_c and M_{c'} be components with H_c ≠ H_{c'}. Both are m-dimensional subspaces of the (m+1)-dimensional A₀, so dim(H_c ∩ H_{c'}) ≥ m + m − (m + 1) = m − 1 ≥ 1; choose w ≠ 0 in H_c ∩ H_{c'}. By step 6, w ∈ M_c ∩ M_{c'}, so M_c = M_{c'} (components are equal or disjoint) and H_c = M_c ∪ {0} = M_{c'} ∪ {0} = H_{c'}, a contradiction. Hence all components have the same subspace H₀ := H_c.

8. (Conclusion.) M ≠ ∅, so M has at least one component, and M is the union of its components: M = H₀ ∖ {0}, with Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m. ∎

subproblem.title: Tangential gradients of locally Lipschitz functions on an embedded C¹ submanifold: a.e.-measurability, and smooth approximation with L²-convergent gradients (parent step 4c)
subproblem.statement: Calculus of locally Lipschitz functions on a C¹ submanifold. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; M ⊆ ℝ^P. Hypothesis: M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M). Notation: d^M_xζ := fderivWithin ℝ ζ M x; P_x is the orthogonal projection onto span(tangentSpace M x); e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1; H^m = μHE[m]. Conclusion (two parts). (i) Measurability: for every ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ that is locally Lipschitz on M (LocallyLipschitzOn M ζ) and every j ∈ Fin P, the function x ↦ d^M_xζ(P_xe_j) is a.e. strongly measurable with respect to H^m restricted to M. (ii) Approximation: for every ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ that is locally Lipschitz on M and vanishes on M outside some compact set C ⊆ M, there are a compact set C' ⊆ M and functions ζ_k : ℝ^P → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ), each C^∞ with compact support, such that ζ_k(x) = 0 for all k and all x ∈ M ∖ C'; ζ_k → ζ uniformly on M (TendstoUniformlyOn ζ_k ζ atTop M); and ∫⁻_M ofReal(Σ_{j=1}^P (Dζ_k(x)(P_xe_j) − d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))²) dH^m(x) → 0 as k → ∞, where Dζ_k(x) = fderiv ℝ ζ_k x.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 4c of the supplied proof of the parent, together with the measurability of tangential gradients of Lipschitz functions used implicitly in its steps 4c and 6 ("Mollify in finitely many charts (partition of unity) to get ζ_k ∈ C^∞_c(M) with supports in a fixed compact K' ⊆ M, ζ_k → ζ uniformly and ∇^Mζ_k → ∇^Mζ in L²(H^m⌞K')"), with Simon Ch. 2, 4.4 (graph representations) and 4.5–4.9 (Rademacher's theorem on M through local coordinates). Here the approximants are produced directly as ambient C^∞ functions. Sibling lemmas: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv), locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed).

Notation. H^m := μHE[m], L^m Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m. For x ∈ M, T_x := tangentSpace M x is an m-dimensional linear subspace (chart_tangent_space) and P_x is its orthogonal projection. For a linear functional ℓ on ℝ^P put |ℓ|²_{T_x} := Σ_j ℓ(P_xe_j)²; it equals |P_x∇ℓ|² (∇ℓ the representing vector) and Σ_i ℓ(τ_i)² for every orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x, so it depends only on ℓ restricted to T_x, and |·|_{T_x} is a seminorm.

Steps 1–7 prove part (ii); step 8 proves part (i).

1. (Graph charts.) Let p ∈ M. Take a C¹ chart (V, W, ψ) of M at p; T_p = range Dψ(ψ^{-1}(p)). Fix a linear isometry ι_p : ℝ^m → ℝ^P onto T_p and put π_p := ι_p*. The map π_p∘(ψ − p) has invertible derivative at ψ^{-1}(p), so by the inverse function theorem (Simon 4.4) there are an open ball D_p ⊆ ℝ^m centred at 0, an open set W_p ∋ p with W_p ⊆ W and a C¹ map G_p : D_p → ℝ^P such that M ∩ W_p = G_p(D_p) and π_p(G_p(a) − p) = a for a ∈ D_p. [G_p := ψ∘(π_p∘(ψ − p))^{-1} on D_p; W_p exists because ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ M — it is continuous, injective, and proper.] Consequences:
 (1a) G_p is a homeomorphism of D_p onto M ∩ W_p with inverse x ↦ π_p(x − p), and |G_p(a) − G_p(b)| ≥ |a − b|.
 (1b) For a ∈ D_p, DG_p(a) is injective with range T_{G_p(a)} (chart_tangent_space and the chain rule), and π_p∘DG_p(a) = id; hence |DG_p(a)h| ≥ |h| and π_p restricted to T_{G_p(a)} is DG_p(a)^{-1}, of norm ≤ 1.
 (1c) For compact K ⊆ W_p, M ∩ K = ψ(V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K)) is compact.
 Since ζ is locally Lipschitz on M and G_p is continuous with G_p(0) = p, we can choose an open ball D'_p centred at 0 with closure in D_p such that ζ is Lipschitz on M ∩ G_p(D'_p). Put W'_p := {z ∈ W_p : π_p(z − p) ∈ D'_p}, an open set with M ∩ W'_p = G_p(D'_p). DG_p is bounded on D'_p (continuous on the compact closure), so G_p is Lipschitz on the convex set D'_p, with a constant Λ_p.

2. (Partition of unity.) The compact set C is covered by the open sets W'_p, p ∈ C; choose p_1, …, p_L with C ⊆ W'_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W'_L, and write D_l, D'_l, W'_l, G_l, π_l, Λ_l for the data of p_l. Choose χ_l ∈ C^∞_c(W'_l; [0, 1]) with Σ_lχ_l = 1 on a neighbourhood of C (a smooth partition of unity subordinate to a finite open cover of a compact set). As ζ = 0 on M ∖ C, ζ = Σ_lχ_lζ on M.

3. (Coordinate functions.) For each l let g_l(a) := χ_l(G_l(a))·ζ(G_l(a)) for a ∈ D'_l and g_l(a) := 0 for a ∉ D'_l. The set S_l := π_l((M ∩ tsupport χ_l) − p_l) is compact (M ∩ tsupport χ_l is compact by (1c), as tsupport χ_l is a compact subset of W'_l ⊆ W_l) and S_l ⊆ D'_l; g_l = 0 off S_l. g_l is Lipschitz on ℝ^m: on D'_l it is the product of the C¹ function χ_l∘G_l (with bounded derivative on D'_l) and the bounded Lipschitz function ζ∘G_l (ζ is Lipschitz on M ∩ W'_l and G_l is Lipschitz on D'_l); S_l has positive distance δ_l from ℝ^m ∖ D'_l, so for a ∈ S_l and b ∉ D'_l, |g_l(a) − g_l(b)| ≤ sup|g_l| ≤ (sup|g_l|/δ_l)|a − b|. Moreover χ_lζ = g_l∘π_l(· − p_l) on M ∩ W'_l, and χ_lζ = 0 on M ∖ W'_l.

4. (Mollification.) Let ϕ be a mollifier on ℝ^m (C^∞, ϕ ≥ 0, support in B_1(0), ∫ϕ = 1), ϕ_ε(a) := ε^{-m}ϕ(a/ε), fix k₀ with 1/k₀ < δ_l/2 for all l, and put g_{l,k} := g_l ∗ ϕ_{1/(k+k₀)} for k ∈ ℕ. Then g_{l,k} ∈ C^∞(ℝ^m), spt g_{l,k} ⊆ S'_l := {a : dist(a, S_l) ≤ δ_l/2}, a compact subset of D'_l, and g_{l,k} → g_l uniformly (g_l is uniformly continuous). By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) g_l is differentiable outside an L^m-null set N_l, with |Dg_l| ≤ Lip(g_l). A Lipschitz function is absolutely continuous on lines, so its distributional gradient is Dg_l; hence Dg_{l,k} = (Dg_l) ∗ ϕ_{1/(k+k₀)} → Dg_l in L²(ℝ^m) (mollification in L² of the bounded, compactly supported Dg_l).

5. (Ambient approximants.) Choose β_l ∈ C^∞_c(W'_l; [0, 1]) with β_l = 1 on a neighbourhood of the compact set G_l(S'_l) ⊆ M ∩ W'_l. Define ζ_k(z) := Σ_{l=1}^L β_l(z)·g_{l,k}(π_l(z − p_l)), each term being taken as 0 outside W'_l. Each term is C^∞ on ℝ^P (β_l has compact support in W'_l, and z ↦ g_{l,k}(π_l(z − p_l)) is C^∞), so ζ_k is C^∞ with compact support. On M: if x ∈ M ∩ W'_l, then π_l(x − p_l) = G_l^{-1}(x) =: a, and either a ∈ S'_l, so x ∈ G_l(S'_l) and β_l(x) = 1, or a ∉ S'_l and g_{l,k}(a) = 0; if x ∈ M ∖ W'_l, the l-th term is 0. Hence, on M,
 ζ_k = Σ_l g_{l,k}∘G_l^{-1}, the l-th term being 0 on M ∖ W'_l.
 Put C' := G_1(S'_1) ∪ ⋯ ∪ G_L(S'_L), a compact subset of M. Then ζ_k = 0 on M ∖ C' for every k.

6. (Uniform convergence.) By step 3, ζ = Σ_l g_l∘G_l^{-1} on M (same convention). So ζ_k − ζ = Σ_l (g_{l,k} − g_l)∘G_l^{-1} on M and sup_M|ζ_k − ζ| ≤ Σ_l sup|g_{l,k} − g_l| → 0.

7. (Tangential derivatives.)
 (7a) Let x ∈ M ∩ W'_l, a := G_l^{-1}(x), and let g : ℝ^m → ℝ be differentiable at a. Then f := g∘π_l(· − p_l) is differentiable within M at x with derivative Dg(a)∘π_l: for y ∈ M near x, f(y) − f(x) = Dg(a)(π_l(y − x)) + o(|π_l(y − x)|) and |π_l(y − x)| ≤ |y − x|. On T_x this derivative is Dg(a)∘DG_l(a)^{-1} (1b), so |Dg(a)∘π_l|_{T_x} ≤ |Dg(a)|.
 (7b) Let N := ⋃_l G_l(N_l ∩ D'_l). G_l is Λ_l-Lipschitz on D'_l, so H^m(G_l(N_l ∩ D'_l)) ≤ Λ_l^m·L^m(N_l) = 0 (Lipschitz images: Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, μHE[m] being a constant multiple of μH[m], and μHE[m] = L^m on ℝ^m); so H^m(N) = 0. Let x ∈ M ∖ N. Each term of ζ = Σ_l g_l∘G_l^{-1} is differentiable within M at x: if x ∈ W'_l, by (7a), since G_l^{-1}(x) ∉ N_l; if x ∉ W'_l, then x ∉ G_l(S_l) (a compact set), and the term vanishes on M near x. Hence ζ is differentiable within M at x, and d^M_xζ = fderivWithin ℝ ζ M x agrees on T_x with the sum of the derivatives of the terms (derivatives within M at x are unique on T_x, which is spanned by velocities of C¹ curves in M through x). Likewise Dζ_k(x) agrees on T_x with the sum of the derivatives of the terms g_{l,k}∘G_l^{-1} (step 5, applied on the neighbourhood M ∩ W'_l of x, resp. vanishing terms).
 (7c) Hence, for x ∈ M ∖ N, by Cauchy–Schwarz over the L terms and (7a),
 |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} ≤ L·Σ_l |D(g_{l,k} − g_l)(G_l^{-1}(x))|²·1_{G_l(S'_l)}(x)
 (the l-th term vanishes on M near x unless x ∈ G_l(S'_l)).
 (7d) For Borel h ≥ 0 on ℝ^m, ∫_{G_l(S'_l)} h(G_l^{-1}(x)) dH^m(x) ≤ Λ_l^m∫_{S'_l} h dL^m: for h = 1_F this is H^m(G_l(F ∩ S'_l)) ≤ Λ_l^mL^m(F ∩ S'_l) (G_l(F ∩ S'_l) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin), and the inequality extends to simple and then to Borel h ≥ 0. Therefore
 ∫⁻_M ofReal(Σ_j (Dζ_k(x)(P_xe_j) − d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))²) dH^m = ∫⁻_M |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} dH^m ≤ L·Σ_l Λ_l^m∫_{S'_l}|D(g_{l,k} − g_l)|² dL^m → 0
 by step 4, using H^m(N) = 0.
 Steps 5–7 give C', the functions ζ_k and the three required properties of part (ii).

8. (Part (i): measurability.) Let ζ be locally Lipschitz on M (no support condition) and j ∈ Fin P. For every p ∈ M, step 1 gives a graph chart G_p : D_p → M ∩ W_p and a smaller ball D'_p with ζ Lipschitz on M ∩ W'_p = G_p(D'_p). As ℝ^P is second countable, countably many of the open sets W'_p, say W'_l := W'_{p_l} (l ∈ ℕ), cover M. Fix l and put g := ζ∘G_l on D'_l; g is Lipschitz on the open ball D'_l (ζ is Lipschitz on M ∩ W'_l and G_l is Lipschitz on D'_l), so by Rademacher's theorem for functions Lipschitz on a set (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem; within the open set D'_l this is differentiability) g is differentiable at every a ∈ D'_l outside an L^m-null set N'_l. The map a ↦ fderiv ℝ g a is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), x ↦ π_l(x − p_l) is continuous, and x ↦ P_x is continuous on M (in chart coordinates P_{G_l(a)} = DG_l(a)(DG_l(a)*DG_l(a))^{-1}DG_l(a)*). Hence Ψ_l(x) := fderiv ℝ g (π_l(x − p_l)) (π_l(P_xe_j)) is a Borel function on M ∩ W'_l. If x ∈ M ∩ W'_l and a := π_l(x − p_l) ∉ N'_l, then ζ = g∘π_l(· − p_l) on the neighbourhood M ∩ W'_l of x in M, so by the argument of (7a) (with the chart G_l of this countable family) ζ is differentiable within M at x with derivative Dg(a)∘π_l, and fderivWithin ℝ ζ M x agrees with it on T_x ∋ P_xe_j; thus d^M_xζ(P_xe_j) = Ψ_l(x). The exceptional set G_l(N'_l) is H^m-null, as in (7b). Define Ψ(x) := Ψ_l(x) for x ∈ (M ∩ W'_l) ∖ (W'_0 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W'_{l−1}) and Ψ := 0 off M. Ψ is Borel and x ↦ d^M_xζ(P_xe_j) equals Ψ at H^m-a.e. point of M, so it is a.e. strongly measurable for H^m restricted to M (ℝ is second countable). ∎

g_l := (χ_lζ)∘G_l is Lipschitz with compact support in the chart ball; mollification gives g_{l,k} → g_l uniformly and Dg_{l,k} → Dg_l in L² (Rademacher).
ζ_k(z) := Σ_l β_l(z)g_{l,k}(π_l(z − p_l)) is ambient C^∞ with compact support, equals Σ_l g_{l,k}∘G_l^{-1} on M and vanishes on M off a fixed compact C'.
Off the H^m-null image of the non-differentiability sets, ζ is differentiable within M; chart gradient errors control tangential gradient errors and Lipschitz images transfer the L² convergence.

subproblem.title: An embedded submanifold that is C^r for every r has C^∞ charts (graph representation over the tangent plane, Simon Ch. 2, 4.4)
subproblem.statement: C^∞ charts. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; M ⊆ ℝ^P. Hypothesis: for every r ∈ ℕ, M is an embedded C^r m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M); the charts may depend on r. Conclusion: every y ∈ M has a C^∞ local representation: there are open sets V ⊆ ℝ^m and W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W and a map ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P that is C^∞ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ V, i.e. of class C^n on V for every n ∈ ℕ), injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) = fderiv ℝ ψ z injective for every z ∈ V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ r : ℕ, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M) → ∀ y ∈ M, ∃ (V : Set (Euclid m)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P), IsOpen V ∧ IsOpen W ∧ y ∈ W ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ V ∧ InjOn ψ V ∧ ψ '' V = W ∩ M ∧ (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) ∧ ∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)
proof_key_steps: A C¹ chart and the inverse function theorem give a C¹ graph G(a) = y + ι(a) + u(a) over T_yM with M ∩ W₀ = G(D) and π(G(a) − y) = a.
At x₀ = G(a₀), a C^r chart ψ' composed with the inverse of π∘(ψ' − y) agrees with G near a₀, so G is C^r near a₀ for every r.
Hence G is C^∞ on D; it is injective, proper and has injective derivative because π(G(a) − y) = a.

subproblem.title: Allard–Schauder regularity: a stationary embedded C¹ submanifold is C^r for every r (Simon Ch. 5, Theorem 7.1, last part; parent step 2)
subproblem.statement: Higher regularity of stationary C¹ submanifolds. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; U ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P. Hypotheses: m ≥ 1; U is open; M ⊆ U; M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M); H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; and M is stationary in U: ∫_M div_M X dH^m = 0 for every C¹ map X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U, where div_M X(x) := trace(P_x∘DX(x)), P_x is the orthogonal projection onto span(tangentSpace M x), and H^m = μHE[m]. Conclusion: for every r ∈ ℕ, M is an embedded C^r m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M : Set (Euclid P)), 1 ≤ m → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[m] (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → (∀ X : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ U → ∫ x in M, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) ((Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x)).starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ (fderiv ℝ X x).toLinearMap) ∂μHE[m] = 0) → ∀ r : ℕ, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 5, Theorem 7.1 and its proof (chapter-05.txt lines 1306–1366), last part: if θ is a positive integer, N is a C^{q+3} submanifold and V is stationary in U ∩ N, then near a point of density one spt V is the graph of a C^{q+2,α} function. This is how step 2 of the supplied proof of the parent obtains smoothness ("for every y ∈ M and every q there are σ > 0 and a rigid motion after which M ∩ B_σ(y) is the graph of a C^{q+2,α} function"). Supporting book results: Ch. 4, 2.6 and 3.14 (stationary varifolds have generalized mean curvature 0); Ch. 3, 1.4–1.8 (approximate tangent spaces and densities). Sibling lemmas: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv: tangentSpace M x = range Dψ(v), the m-dimensional classical tangent plane), density_one (Submission.dimred_rpd_submanifold_density_one), locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed).

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; B_s(x) := ball x s; ω_m := unitBallVolume m; T_xM := tangentSpace M x.

1. (Orders r ≤ 1.) A C¹ chart is a C^r chart for r ≤ 1 (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 implies ContDiffOn ℝ r), so IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M holds for r ≤ 1. Fix r ≥ 2 and y ∈ M. We construct a C^r chart of M at y.

2. (Local closedness.) By locally_closed, part (b), there is ε > 0 with M ∩ closedBall(y, ε) compact. Choose ρ > 0 with 2ρ < ε and closedBall(y, 2ρ) ⊆ U, and put B := B_{2ρ}(y). For every compact K ⊆ B, M ∩ K = (M ∩ closedBall(y, ε)) ∩ K is compact. In particular M ∩ B is relatively closed in B.

3. (The varifold and its first variation.) Let V₀ := v(M ∩ B, 1), the rectifiable m-varifold in B with multiplicity θ ≡ 1 on M ∩ B. M ∩ B is an embedded C¹ submanifold (restrict the charts of M to the open set B), hence Borel and countably m-rectifiable, and μ_{V₀} = H^m⌞(M ∩ B) is a Radon measure on B, since H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B ⊆ U. At every x ∈ M ∩ B the approximate tangent space of V₀ is T_xM = tangentSpace M x = range Dψ(v) for any chart ψ with ψ(v) = x (chart_tangent_space): near x, M is the graph over T_xM of a C¹ function with zero derivative at x (inverse function theorem applied to the orthogonal projection onto T_xM of a chart, Simon Ch. 2, 4.4), so the blow-ups λ^{-1}(M − x) converge locally to T_xM as C¹ graphs with gradients tending to 0, and η_{x,λ#}(H^m⌞M) → H^m⌞T_xM (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 and 1.7). Hence, for X ∈ C¹_c(B; ℝ^P), the first variation of V₀ is δV₀(X) = ∫_{M∩B} div_M X dH^m (Simon Ch. 4, 2.2, with div_M computed on T_xM). For such X, tsupport X ⊆ B ⊆ U and div_M X = 0 on M ∖ B (DX = 0 outside tsupport X), so δV₀(X) = ∫_M div_M X dH^m = 0 by the stationarity hypothesis. Thus V₀ is stationary in B (Simon Ch. 4, 2.6, with N = ℝ^P); equivalently it has generalized mean curvature H = 0 in B (Ch. 4, 3.14), and in particular H ∈ L^p_loc(μ_{V₀}) for every p > m.

4. (Density.) By density_one, Θ^m(V₀, x) = lim_{s↓0} H^m(M ∩ B_s(x))/(ω_m s^m) = 1 for every x ∈ M ∩ B. Thus θ ≡ 1 ≥ 1 and Θ^m(V₀, y) = 1. Moreover spt μ_{V₀} ∩ B = M ∩ B: every point of M ∩ B has positive density, hence lies in the support, and M ∩ B is closed in B (step 2).

5. (Allard–Schauder.) The hypotheses of Simon Ch. 5, Theorem 7.1 hold in the open set B at the point ξ := y: V₀ = v(M ∩ B, θ) has generalized mean curvature H = 0, which is locally in L^p for some p > m; θ ≥ 1 and θ is positive integer-valued; Θ^m(V₀, y) = 1; and V₀ is stationary in B ∩ N with N := ℝ^P, a C^∞ (in particular C^{q+3}) submanifold of dimension P (step 3). Apply the last part of Theorem 7.1 with q := r. Together with formula (1) of its proof (graph u = spt V ∩ B_σ(0), after translating by −y and applying an orthogonal transformation), it gives σ ∈ (0, ρ), an orthogonal transformation Q of ℝ^P, an open set Ω ⊆ ℝ^m with 0 ∈ Ω and u ∈ C^{r+2,α}(Ω; ℝ^{P−m}) ⊆ C^r(Ω; ℝ^{P−m}) with u(0) = 0 and Du(0) = 0, such that
 Q(spt μ_{V₀} − y) ∩ B_σ(0) = {(a, u(a)) : a ∈ Ω}.
 Since σ < 2ρ, spt μ_{V₀} ∩ B_σ(y) = M ∩ B_σ(y) by step 4. Hence M ∩ B_σ(y) = {y + Q^{-1}(a, u(a)) : a ∈ Ω}.

6. (A C^r chart at y.) Define linear isometries ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, ι(a) := Q^{-1}(a, 0), and ι' : ℝ^{P−m} → ℝ^P, ι'(b) := Q^{-1}(0, b), with orthogonal ranges, and put π := ι* (so π∘ι = id and π∘ι' = 0). Let G(a) := y + ι(a) + ι'(u(a)) for a ∈ Ω and G(a) := y + ι(a) for a ∉ Ω. Take V₁ := Ω, W₁ := B_σ(y) and ψ := G. Then:
 (i) V₁ and W₁ are open, and y = G(0) ∈ W₁;
 (ii) G is C^r on V₁, because u ∈ C^r(Ω);
 (iii) G is injective on V₁, because π(G(a) − y) = a;
 (iv) G(V₁) = M ∩ B_σ(y) = W₁ ∩ M, by step 5;
 (v) for every compact K ⊆ W₁, V₁ ∩ G^{-1}(K) = π((M ∩ K) − y): if a ∈ V₁ and G(a) ∈ K, then G(a) ∈ M ∩ K and a = π(G(a) − y); conversely each z ∈ M ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ B_σ(y) is z = G(a) with a ∈ V₁, and π(z − y) = a. M ∩ K is compact by step 2 (K ⊆ B), so V₁ ∩ G^{-1}(K) is compact;
 (vi) DG(a) = ι + ι'∘Du(a) satisfies π∘DG(a) = id, so DG(a) is injective for a ∈ V₁.
 The values of G outside the open set V₁ affect neither ContDiffOn on V₁ nor fderiv at points of V₁. Hence (V₁, W₁, G) is a C^r chart of M at y in the sense of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M. As y ∈ M was arbitrary, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M holds, for every r ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: For r ≤ 1 the C¹ charts suffice; for r ≥ 2 fix y ∈ M and a ball B = B_{2ρ}(y) ⊆ U in which M is relatively closed (locally_closed).
v(M ∩ B, 1) is stationary in B, its first variation being ∫_M div_M X dH^m, and has density 1 at every point of M ∩ B (density_one); its support in B is M ∩ B.
Simon Ch. 5, Theorem 7.1, last part (N = ℝ^P, q = r) and formula (1) of its proof: after a rigid motion, M ∩ B_σ(y) is the graph of a C^{r+2,α} function u.
G(a) = y + ι(a) + ι'(u(a)) is a C^r chart at y: injective, proper, with injective derivative and image W ∩ M.

Hypotheses: U is open; M ⊆ U; M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M); H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; and for every C^∞ map Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport Z ⊆ U there is t₀ > 0 such that H^m(M ∩ tsupport Z) ≤ H^m({x + tZ(x) : x ∈ M ∩ tsupport Z}) for every t with |t| < t₀. Conclusion: for every C¹ map X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U, ∫_M div_M X dH^m = 0, where div_M X(x) := trace(P_x∘DX(x)), P_x is the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto span(tangentSpace M x) (starProjection), DX(x) = fderiv ℝ X x, and the integral is the Bochner integral over M with respect to H^m = μHE[m].

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 5.1–5.3 (area formula for the deformations φ_t = id + tZ, Taylor expansion of J_t, first variation formula 5.3 and the definition of stationarity after 5.4); steps (0c) and 1 of the supplied proof of the parent. Sibling lemmas: area_formula (Submission.codim1_hcp_submanifold_area_formula), chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv), locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed).

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; T_x := tangentSpace M x; P_x as in the statement; div_M X(x) := trace(P_x∘DX(x)).

0. (Preliminaries.)
 (0.1) M is Borel (locally_closed, part (a)). For x ∈ M choose a chart (V, W, ψ) of M with x = ψ(v); chart_tangent_space gives T_x = range Dψ(v), an m-dimensional linear subspace (Dψ(v) is injective). So span(T_x) = T_x and P_x is the orthogonal projection onto T_x.
 (0.2) (Trace formula.) For every linear L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and every orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x, trace(P_x∘L) = Σ_{i=1}^m τ_i·Lτ_i. Indeed, extend τ to an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_P of ℝ^P; then trace(P_xL) = Σ_{j≤P} τ_j·P_xLτ_j = Σ_j P_xτ_j·Lτ_j = Σ_{i≤m} τ_i·Lτ_i. In particular |div_M X(x)| ≤ m‖DX(x)‖.
 (0.3) (Continuity along M.) In a chart, P_{ψ(v)} = Dψ(v)(Dψ(v)*Dψ(v))^{-1}Dψ(v)* is a continuous function of v ∈ V, and ψ^{-1} : W ∩ M → V is continuous (if ψ(z_j) → ψ(z), the compact set {ψ(z_j)} ∪ {ψ(z)} ⊆ W has a compact preimage in V containing every z_j, and every cluster point of (z_j) equals z by injectivity). Hence x ↦ P_x is continuous on M, and for every X with continuous DX the function x ↦ div_M X(x) is continuous on M; as M is Borel, 1_M·div_M X is Borel.

1. (Set-up.) Fix a C^∞ map Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support K := tsupport Z ⊆ U, and put Λ := sup_{ℝ^P}‖DZ‖ < ∞ (DZ is continuous with compact support). If K = ∅ then Z ≡ 0 and (1.1) below is trivial, so assume K ≠ ∅.

2. (Deformations.) For t ∈ ℝ let Φ_t(x) := x + tZ(x). If |t|Λ < 1, then Φ_t is C^∞ with DΦ_t(x) = I + tDZ(x), which is injective because ‖tDZ(x)‖ < 1; and Φ_t is injective, because the mean value inequality gives |Z(a) − Z(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b| and hence |Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| ≥ (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b|.

3. (Area formula.) For |t| < 1/(1 + Λ), area_formula applied to M, the Borel set E := M ∩ K ⊆ M and Φ := Φ_t gives
 f(t) := H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^m, J_t(x) := √det G_t(x), G_t(x) := (DΦ_t(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ_t(x)∘ι_x),
 ι_x : T_x → ℝ^P the inclusion. In an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x the matrix of G_t(x) is b_ij(t) = (τ_i + tDZ(x)τ_i)·(τ_j + tDZ(x)τ_j) = δ_ij + t c_ij + t² d_ij, with c_ij := τ_i·DZ(x)τ_j + τ_j·DZ(x)τ_i and d_ij := DZ(x)τ_i·DZ(x)τ_j; |c_ij| ≤ 2Λ and |d_ij| ≤ Λ².

4. (Uniform bounds in t.) g(t, x) := det G_t(x) = det(δ_ij + tc_ij + t²d_ij) is a polynomial in t of degree ≤ 2m whose coefficients are polynomials in the c_ij and d_ij. Hence there are constants C_k = C_k(m, Λ) with |∂_t^k g(t, x)| ≤ C_k for |t| ≤ 1 and x ∈ M, and g(0, x) = 1. Choose t₁ ∈ (0, 1/(1 + Λ)) with C_1t₁ ≤ 1/2. Then g(t, x) ≥ 1/2 for |t| ≤ t₁, so J_t(x) = √g(t, x) is C^∞ in t on (−t₁, t₁), with |∂_tJ_t(x)| ≤ C_1/√2 and 0 ≤ J_t(x) ≤ √(1 + C_1) for all such t and all x ∈ M ∩ K. By Jacobi's formula (the derivative of det at the identity is the trace) and (0.2),
 ∂_tJ_t(x)|_{t=0} = ½∂_tg(0, x) = ½Σ_i c_ii = Σ_i τ_i·DZ(x)τ_i = div_M Z(x).

5. (Differentiation under the integral sign.) For each t, J_t is continuous on M ∩ K (as in (0.3): in a chart, G_t is a continuous function of v), hence Borel there. H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ because K is a compact subset of U. So F(t) := ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^m is a finite real number and f(t) = ENNReal.ofReal(F(t)) for |t| < t₁. The bound of step 4 is an integrable dominant on M ∩ K, so by differentiation under the integral sign (Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le) F is differentiable at 0 with F'(0) = ∫_{M∩K} div_M Z dH^m.

6. (Minimality.) By hypothesis there is t₀ > 0 with f(0) = H^m(M ∩ K) ≤ f(t) for |t| < t₀ (Φ_0 = id). Hence F(0) ≤ F(t) for |t| < min(t₀, t₁): F has a local minimum at the interior point 0, where it is differentiable, so F'(0) = 0 (Fermat). Thus ∫_{M∩K} div_M Z dH^m = 0.

7. (Off K.) Z ≡ 0 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K, so DZ = 0 there and div_M Z = 0 on M ∖ K. div_M Z is Borel on M, bounded by mΛ, and vanishes off M ∩ K, a set of finite measure; so it is integrable on M and
 (1.1) ∫_M div_M Z dH^m = ∫_{M∩K} div_M Z dH^m = 0.

8. (C¹ vector fields.) Let X be C¹ with compact support K₀ := tsupport X ⊆ U. Since K₀ is compact and U is open, there is δ > 0 with K' := {x : dist(x, K₀) ≤ δ} ⊆ U; K' is compact. Let ϕ ∈ C^∞_c(B_1(0)) with ϕ ≥ 0 and ∫ϕ = 1, ϕ_k(x) := k^Pϕ(kx), and X_k := X ∗ ϕ_k for k > 1/δ. Then X_k is C^∞, tsupport X_k ⊆ K' ⊆ U is compact, and DX_k = (DX) ∗ ϕ_k → DX uniformly on ℝ^P because DX is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support). By (1.1) with Z := X_k, ∫_M div_M X_k dH^m = 0 for every k > 1/δ. For x ∈ M, |div_M X_k(x) − div_M X(x)| ≤ m·sup‖DX_k − DX‖ → 0 by (0.2); |div_M X_k| ≤ m·sup‖DX‖; div_M X_k and div_M X vanish on M ∖ K'; and H^m(M ∩ K') < ∞. Dominated convergence gives ∫_M div_M X dH^m = lim_k ∫_M div_M X_k dH^m = 0. Since P_x is the starProjection of span(tangentSpace M x) and DX(x) = fderiv ℝ X x, this is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: For |t|·sup‖DZ‖ < 1, Φ_t = id + tZ is an injective C^∞ map with injective derivative.

det G_t is a polynomial in t with uniformly bounded coefficients, ≥ 1/2 for |t| ≤ t₁, and ∂_tJ_t|_{t=0} = div_M Z.
Differentiate under the integral; the deformation hypothesis gives a local minimum at 0, so ∫_M div_M Z dH^m = 0 (div_M Z = 0 off K).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Appendix B: B.4–B.11 and the printed proof of B.2 (chapter-B.txt lines 88–282 = chapter-07-source.txt lines 1340–1539), as organized in steps 3 (homogeneity of ν), 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the supplied proof of the parent. The finite-dimensional algebra of B.10–B.11 is kernel-checked in SimonGMT: Poincare.SimonGMT.AppendixB.simonsDefect_eq_sum_skew, four_mul_radialSkewSum_le, radial_derivative_of_codazzi, cone_simonsDefect_lower_bound; the exponent is AppendixB.exists_final_exponent (ε = 1/10). Departures, stated explicitly: (i) the printed proof obtains the finiteness of the integrals in (4) and (6) from the polar formula (5) ∫_M f dH^m = ∫_0^∞ r^{m−1}∫_Σ f(rω) dH^{m−1}(ω) dr; only these finiteness statements and the H^m-nullity of M ∩ {r = 1} are used, and they are proved below by dyadic scaling of H^m, which avoids the (m−1)-dimensional area formula on Σ; (ii) as printed, the second line of B.7 carries the opposite sign on the two curvature terms relative to its first line and B.6; Simons' identity is derived below with one fixed convention, and it coincides with the printed B.8 (whose printed proof uses the correct signs); (iii) the cut-off parameter of the printed text, also called ε there, is called κ. Sibling lemmas: smooth_charts (Submission.codim1_hcp_smooth_charts), lipschitz_approx (Submission.codim1_hcp_lipschitz_smooth_approx), chart_tangent_space, density_one (Submission.dimred_rpd_submanifold_density_one), locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed).

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; r(x) := |x|; U₀ := ℝ^P ∖ {0}; T_x := tangentSpace M x, P_x its orthogonal projection; D_τν := Dν(x)τ; for a linear functional ℓ, |ℓ|²_{T_x} := Σ_jℓ(P_xe_j)² (= Σ_iℓ(τ_i)² for an orthonormal basis τ of T_x). If M = ∅ there is nothing to prove; assume M ≠ ∅.

0. (Preliminaries.)
 (0a) Cone and closure. Applying the cone property with t and 1/t gives tM = M for t > 0. Since 0 ∉ M and closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0}, M is closed in U₀, and for 0 < a ≤ b the set M ∩ {a ≤ r ≤ b} = closure(M) ∩ {a ≤ r ≤ b} is compact. So a function vanishing on M outside M ∩ {a ≤ r ≤ b} vanishes outside a compact subset of M.
 (0b) Tangent spaces. For x ∈ M, T_x is an m-dimensional linear subspace (chart_tangent_space), T_x ⊆ A₀ (velocities of curves in M ⊆ A₀), A₀ = T_x ⊕ ℝν(x) orthogonally, x ∈ T_x (s ↦ e^sx is a C¹ curve in M through x with velocity x), and T_{tx} = T_x for t > 0 (if γ is a C¹ curve in M through x then tγ is one through tx, so tT_x ⊆ T_{tx}, and symmetrically). Hence P_x(x/|x|) = x/|x|, and for f(z) = g(|z|) with g C¹ near |x|, |Df(x)|_{T_x} = |g'(|x|)|.
 (0c) Second fundamental form. For x ∈ M and τ, η ∈ T_x: D_τν ∈ T_x (differentiate ν(γ(s)) ∈ A₀ and |ν(γ(s))|² = 1 along a C¹ curve γ in M with γ'(0) = τ, and use (0b)); and η·D_τν = τ·D_ην (in a C^∞ chart ψ of M (smooth_charts), differentiate ν(ψ(v))·∂_iψ(v) = 0 in v_j; the term ν·∂_j∂_iψ is symmetric). With an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x and h_ij := −τ_j·D_{τ_i}ν = h_ji: D_{τ_i}ν = −Σ_jh_ijτ_j; |A|²(x) = Σ_j|Dν(x)(P_xe_j)|² = Σ_i|D_{τ_i}ν|² = Σ_{i,j}h_ij² (Hilbert–Schmidt identity Σ_j|LP_xe_j|² = Σ_i|Lτ_i|²); and H := Σ_ih_ii = −trace(P_xDν(x)) = 0.
 (0d) Homogeneity (parent step 3). For x ∈ M and t > 0, ν(tx) = ν(x): ν(tx) is a unit vector of A₀ ∩ T_{tx}^⊥ = A₀ ∩ T_x^⊥ = ℝν(x), so ν(tx) = ±ν(x), and t ↦ ν(tx)·ν(x) is continuous on (0, ∞) with values in {±1} and value 1 at t = 1. Differentiating ν(tγ(s)) = ν(γ(s)) at s = 0 along C¹ curves γ in M through x gives t·Dν(tx)τ = Dν(x)τ for τ ∈ T_x. Hence, computed in the same orthonormal basis of T_{tx} = T_x, h_ij(tx) = t^{-1}h_ij(x) and |A|²(tx) = t^{-2}|A|²(x); and D_xν = d/dt ν(tx)|_{t=1} = 0.
 (0e) Measure facts. (i) H^m(tE) = t^mH^m(E) for E ⊆ ℝ^P and t > 0 (scaling of Hausdorff measure). (ii) a₀ := H^m(M ∩ {1 ≤ r < 2}) < ∞ (the closed annulus is compact), and H^m(M ∩ {2^k ≤ r < 2^{k+1}}) = 2^{km}a₀ for every k ∈ ℤ, by (i) and 2^kM = M. (iii) H^m(M ∩ {r = c}) = 0 for every c > 0: the sets M ∩ {r = c}, 1 ≤ c ≤ 2, are pairwise disjoint subsets of a set of finite measure, so at most countably many have positive measure, while H^m(M ∩ {r = c}) = c^mH^m(M ∩ {r = 1}) by (i). (iv) Every nonempty relatively open subset of M has positive H^m-measure: for x ∈ M, H^m(M ∩ B_s(x))/(ω_ms^m) → 1 as s ↓ 0 (density_one).
 (0f) Regularity of |A|. For y ∈ M, smooth_charts and the inverse function theorem (Simon 2, 4.4, applied to the orthogonal projection onto T_y of a C^∞ chart) give a C^∞ graph chart G : D → M ∩ W (D ⊆ ℝ^m an open ball, W ∋ y open, M ∩ W = G(D)) whose inverse is the restriction to M ∩ W of an affine 1-Lipschitz map.  (0g) Calculus on M. For f smooth along M, d^M_xf is its derivative along M (unique on T_x), ∇^Mf(x) ∈ T_x represents it, the divergence of a smooth tangent field Y along M is div_MY(x) := Σ_iτ_i·D_{τ_i}Y (derivatives along curves in M), and Δ_Mf := div_M∇^Mf (the Laplace–Beltrami operator, = Σ_kf_{;kk} in an orthonormal frame). A locally Lipschitz function on M is differentiable within M at H^m-a.e. point of M (Rademacher's theorem in the coordinates of the graph charts, Simon 2, 4.8–4.9: G is locally Lipschitz, so it maps L^m-null sets to H^m-null sets); at such points fderivWithin ℝ f M x is a derivative within M, unique on T_x, and the product and chain rules hold. If f ≥ 0 is locally Lipschitz on M, f(x) = 0 and f is differentiable within M at x, then d^M_xf = 0 on T_x (x is a minimum and every τ ∈ T_x is the velocity of a C¹ curve in M through x). Measurability: for every f locally Lipschitz on M and every j, x ↦ fderivWithin ℝ f M x (P_xe_j) is H^m-a.e. strongly measurable on M (lipschitz_approx, part (i)); hence every integrand below that is built from |A|, r, ψ and tangential derivatives of locally Lipschitz functions is a.e.-measurable on M, and the bounded ones with support in a compact subset of M are integrable.

1. (Simons' identity B.8; Simon B.4–B.9.) Near x₀ ∈ M take a smooth orthonormal frame τ_1, …, τ_m of tangent fields along M (Gram–Schmidt applied to ∂_jG). Let ∇_XY := P(D_XY) be the Levi-Civita connection of M, R(X, Y)Z := ∇_X∇_YZ − ∇_Y∇_XZ − ∇_{[X,Y]}Z its curvature, S the shape operator SX := −D_Xν (tangent by (0c)), so h(X, Y) = SX·Y. Write h_{ij;k} := (∇_{τ_k}h)(τ_i, τ_j) and h_{ij;kl} := (∇²_{τ_l,τ_k}h)(τ_i, τ_j), where ∇²_{X,Y} := ∇_X∇_Y − ∇_{∇_XY} (so k is differentiated first); repeated indices are summed. All fields are A₀-valued and A₀ = T_x ⊕ ℝν(x), so for tangent fields Y, Z: D_YZ = ∇_YZ + h(Y, Z)ν (differentiate ν·Z = 0 along Y).
 B.4 h_ij = h_ji ((0c)); hence h_{ij;k} and h_{ij;kl} are symmetric in i, j.
 B.5/B.6 (Codazzi and Gauss). Flatness of ℝ^P gives D_XD_YZ − D_YD_XZ − D_{[X,Y]}Z = 0. Expanding with D_YZ = ∇_YZ + h(Y, Z)ν and D_Xν = −SX, the normal component gives (∇_Xh)(Y, Z) = (∇_Yh)(X, Z) (Codazzi; with B.4, h_{ij;k} is totally symmetric), and the tangential component gives R(X, Y)Z = h(Y, Z)SX − h(X, Z)SY (Gauss; in components R(τ_i, τ_j)τ_k·τ_l = h_jkh_il − h_ikh_jl, so the sectional curvatures are h_iih_jj − h_ij², as in B.6).
 B.7 (Ricci identity, the definition of R on tensors): h_{ij;kl} − h_{ij;lk} = −h(R(τ_l, τ_k)τ_i, τ_j) − h(τ_i, R(τ_l, τ_k)τ_j).
 Commutation. By B.7 and Gauss, with Sτ_a = h_abτ_b: Σ_k(h_{ki;jk} − h_{ki;kj}) = −h(R(τ_k, τ_j)τ_k, τ_i) − h(τ_k, R(τ_k, τ_j)τ_i) = −[(h³)_ji − H(h²)_ji] − [|A|²h_ji − (h³)_ij] = H(h²)_ij − |A|²h_ij.
 Simons' identity. h_{ij;kk} = h_{ik;jk} (Codazzi, differentiated) = h_{ki;jk} (B.4) = h_{ki;kj} + H(h²)_ij − |A|²h_ij (commutation) = H_{;ij} + H(h²)_ij − |A|²h_ij (Codazzi: Σ_kh_{ki;k} = Σ_kh_{kk;i} = H_{;i}). Multiplying by h_ij and using ½Δ_M|A|² = ½(h_ij²)_{;kk} = h_ijh_{ij;kk} + Σh²_{ij;k}:
 (B.8) ½Δ_M|A|² = Σ_{i,j,k}h²_{ij;k} − |A|⁴ + h_ijH_{;ij} + H·h_mih_mjh_ij.
 Since H ≡ 0 on M ((0c)), ½Δ_M|A|² = Σh²_{ij;k} − |A|⁴. (Check: for the unit sphere, h = δ gives Δh = 0, consistent with the formula h_{ij;kk} = H_{;ij} + H(h²)_ij − |A|²h_ij.)

2. (Lemma B.11.) Let x ∈ M with |A|(x) > 0 and put D := Σ_{i,j,k}h²_{ij;k} − |A|^{-2}Σ_k(Σ_{i,j}h_ijh_{ij;k})². Then D ≥ 2r^{-2}|A|² at x. Proof as printed:
 - Choose the frame near x so that τ_m(z) = z/|z| and τ_1, …, τ_{m−1} are constant along rays (possible by (0b): T_{tz} = T_z ∋ z; take a smooth orthonormal tangent frame e_1, …, e_m near x/|x|, project e_i(z/|z|) onto z^⊥, select m − 1 of these that are independent at x and apply Gram–Schmidt; all operations depend on z/|z| only).
 - (1) h_mj = h_jm = 0 on the ray ℓ_x, because D_{τ_m}ν = |z|^{-1}D_zν = 0 by (0d).
 - (2) h_{ij;m} = −r^{-1}h_ij on ℓ_x: along ℓ_x the frame is constant, so ∇_{τ_m}τ_i = P(D_{τ_m}τ_i) = 0 and h_{ij;m} = τ_m(h_ij) = d/ds h_ij(x + sx/|x|)|_{s=0} = −|x|^{-1}h_ij(x), by h_ij(tx) = t^{-1}h_ij(x) in this frame ((0d)).
 - The algebra: D = ½|A|^{-2}Σ_kΣ_{i,j,r,s}(h_rsh_{ij;k} − h_ijh_{rs;k})² ≥ 2|A|^{-2}Σ_kΣ_{i,j,r<m}(h_ijh_{rm;k})² (the four placements of one radial index; terms containing h_rm vanish by (1)), and Codazzi with (2) gives h_rm;k = h_rk;m = −r^{-1}h_rk, so D ≥ 2r^{-2}|A|^{-2}Σ_{i,j}h_ij²Σ_{r,k}h_rk² = 2r^{-2}|A|² by (1). In SimonGMT terms (index set Fin m = Fin (n + 1), n := m − 1, last index radial, h := (h_ij(x)), dh := (h_{ij;k}(x)), ρ := r(x)): the hypotheses h_last_left, h_last_right are (1), h_flip and dh_flip are B.4, dh_radial is radial_derivative_of_codazzi applied to Codazzi and (2), and cone_simonsDefect_lower_bound gives 2ρ^{-2}·secondFundamentalNormSq h ≤ simonsDefect h dh = D.

3. (Inequality (1) of the printed proof.) H^m-a.e. on M,
 (1) ½Δ_M|A|² + |A|⁴ ≥ 2r^{-2}|A|² + |∇^M|A||².
 Where |A| > 0 (relatively open), |A| is smooth and ∇_k|A| = |A|^{-1}Σ_{ij}h_ijh_{ij;k}, so |∇^M|A||² = |A|^{-2}Σ_k(Σ_{ij}h_ijh_{ij;k})² and (1) is B.8 (with H = 0) combined with Lemma B.11. At points with |A| = 0 at which |A| is differentiable within M (H^m-a.e. such point, by (0f), (0g)), ∇^M|A| = 0 by the minimum principle of (0g), and ½Δ_M|A|² = Σh²_{ij;k} ≥ 0 = 2r^{-2}|A|² + |∇^M|A||² − |A|⁴.

4. (Inequality (3) of the printed proof.) Let ψ be locally Lipschitz on M and vanish on M outside a compact subset of M. Then
 (3) 2∫_M r^{-2}ψ²|A|² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |A|²|∇^Mψ|² dH^m.
 (4a) ζ := |A|ψ (with |A|(x) := (Σ_j|Dν(x)(P_xe_j)|²)^{1/2}) is locally Lipschitz on M ((0f)) and vanishes on M outside a compact subset of M, so B.1 gives
 (2) ∫_M |A|⁴ψ² ≤ ∫_M |∇^M(|A|ψ)|² = ∫_M (|∇^Mψ|²|A|² + ψ²|∇^M|A||² + 2ψ|A|∇^Mψ·∇^M|A|),
 using the product rule at the H^m-a.e. points where |A| and ψ are both differentiable within M ((0g)). All integrands are bounded with support in a compact subset of M (finite measure); r^{-2} is bounded there.
 (4b) H^m-a.e. on M, |A|∇^M|A| = ∇^M(½|A|²): where |A| > 0 by the chain rule; where |A| = 0 (and |A| is differentiable within M) both sides vanish ((0g); ½|A|² is smooth along M with a minimum there). Hence 2ψ|A|∇^Mψ·∇^M|A| = ∇^M(ψ²)·∇^M(½|A|²) a.e.
 (4c) Integration by parts: with f := ½|A|², ∫_M (∇^M(ψ²)·∇^Mf + ψ²Δ_Mf) dH^m = 0. Indeed, ψ² is locally Lipschitz on M and vanishes on M outside a compact set, so lipschitz_approx gives a compact C'' ⊆ M and C^∞ functions χ_k with χ_k = 0 on M ∖ C'', χ_k → ψ² uniformly on M and ∫⁻_M |Dχ_k − d^M(ψ²)|²_{T_x} dH^m → 0. Cover the compact set C'' by finitely many chart cylinders O_l := {z ∈ W_l : π_l(z − p_l) ∈ D_l} ⊆ O ∩ U₀ of C^∞ graph charts G_l : D_l → M ∩ W_l (as in (0f), with inverse π_l(· − p_l)), choose β_l ∈ C^∞_c(O_l) with Σ_lβ_l = 1 on a neighbourhood of C'', and let V_l(z) := ∇^Mf(G_l(π_l(z − p_l))) for z ∈ O_l (C^∞ on O_l, equal to ∇^Mf on M ∩ O_l). Then X_k := χ_k·Σ_lβ_lV_l (each term 0 off O_l) is C^∞ with compact support, 0 ∉ tsupport X_k, and X_k = χ_k∇^Mf on M (near C'' because Σ_lβ_l = 1, and both sides vanish on M ∖ C''). Along M, DX_k(x)τ_i = (Dχ_k(x)τ_i)∇^Mf(x) + χ_k(x)D_{τ_i}(∇^Mf), so div_M X_k = Dχ_k(x)(∇^Mf(x)) + χ_kΔ_Mf. Stationarity gives ∫_M (Dχ_k(∇^Mf) + χ_kΔ_Mf) dH^m = 0. As k → ∞, Dχ_k(x)(∇^Mf(x)) → d^M_x(ψ²)(∇^Mf(x)) in L¹(H^m⌞M) (|Dχ_k(∇^Mf) − d^M(ψ²)(∇^Mf)| ≤ |Dχ_k − d^M(ψ²)|_{T_x}|∇^Mf|, ∇^Mf is bounded on C'' ∪ spt ψ, and these sets have finite measure), and χ_kΔ_Mf → ψ²Δ_Mf uniformly with supports in a fixed compact set. Hence the claim.
 (4d) By (4b), (4c) and (1) (multiplied by ψ² ≥ 0 and integrated),
 2∫_M ψ|A|∇^Mψ·∇^M|A| = ∫_M ∇^M(ψ²)·∇^M(½|A|²) = −∫_M ψ²Δ_M(½|A|²) ≤ ∫_M ψ²(|A|⁴ − 2r^{-2}|A|² − |∇^M|A||²).
 Inserting this into (2) and cancelling the finite quantities ∫ψ²|A|⁴ and ∫ψ²|∇^M|A||² gives (3).

5. (Extension of (3); printed text after (3).) (3) holds for every ψ locally Lipschitz on M such that r^{-2}ψ²|A|² and |A|²|∇^Mψ|² are integrable on M (with respect to H^m), in particular
 (4) ∫_M r^{-2}ψ²|A|² dH^m < ∞.
 (The printed text assumes only (4); if ∫_M |A|²|∇^Mψ|² dH^m = ∞ the inequality is trivial for integrals in [0, ∞], and step 6 checks both integrability conditions for the ψ used.) For 0 < κ < 1 let γ_κ(x) := g_κ(|x|), where g_κ is continuous and piecewise linear: 0 on [0, κ/2], 1 on [κ, κ^{-1}], 0 on [2κ^{-1}, ∞), linear on [κ/2, κ] and on [κ^{-1}, 2κ^{-1}]. Apply (3) to ψγ_κ and use |∇^M(ψγ_κ)|² ≤ (1 + η)|∇^Mψ|²γ_κ² + (1 + η^{-1})ψ²|∇^Mγ_κ|² (a.e., η > 0):
 2∫_M r^{-2}ψ²γ_κ²|A|² ≤ (1 + η)∫_M |A|²|∇^Mψ|² + 9(1 + η^{-1})∫_{M∩E_κ} r^{-2}ψ²|A|².
 Let κ = κ_j ↓ 0. On M, γ_{κ_j} → 1 and 1_{E_{κ_j}} → 0 pointwise (0 < |x| < ∞), and r^{-2}ψ²|A|² is integrable by (4); dominated convergence gives 2∫_M r^{-2}ψ²|A|² ≤ (1 + η)∫_M |A|²|∇^Mψ|². Let η ↓ 0.

6. (Choice of ψ; printed (6).) Let ε := 1/10 (the witness used in SimonGMT AppendixB.exists_final_exponent); for 2 ≤ m ≤ 6, m/2 − 2 + ε ∈ {−0.9, −0.4, 0.1, 0.6, 1.1}, so (m/2 − 2 + ε)² ≤ 1.21 < 2, and (1 + ε)² = 1.21 < 2. So |A|² ≡ 0 on M, i.e. Σ_i|D_{τ_i}ν|² = 0 at every x ∈ M ((0c)), and Dν(x)v = 0 for every v ∈ T_x = tangentSpace M x. ∎

Stability inequality (Simon B.1). Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; U ⊆ ℝ^P; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P; ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P.  ∫_M |A|²(x)ζ(x)² dH^m(x) ≤ ∫_M |∇^Mζ|²(x) dH^m(x),

Source. Step 4 of the supplied proof of the parent — (4a) the variation field Z = ζν, (4b) the second variation (Simon Ch. 2, 5.4, with Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.12 (‡)), (4c) the extension to locally Lipschitz ζ — together with the items of its step 3 on the second fundamental form (D_τν ∈ T_xM, B = hν, |A|² = Σ_i|D_{τ_i}ν|², symmetry by Simon 4.26). Departure: Simon's Lemma 5.11 is used in the pointwise form valid for a variation with zero acceleration, normal initial velocity and H ≡ 0, derived directly from the Taylor expansion of J_t (Simon 5.2–5.4); this needs neither (closure(M) ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅ nor stationarity (Lemma 5.11 uses stationarity only to drop ∫div_M of the acceleration, which is 0 here). Sibling lemmas: area_formula (Submission.codim1_hcp_submanifold_area_formula), lipschitz_approx (Submission.codim1_hcp_lipschitz_smooth_approx), smooth_charts (Submission.codim1_hcp_smooth_charts), chart_tangent_space, locally_closed.

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; T_x := tangentSpace M x and P_x its orthogonal projection (for x ∈ M, T_x is an m-dimensional subspace by chart_tangent_space, so span T_x = T_x); D_τν := Dν(x)τ; for a linear functional ℓ, |ℓ|²_{T_x} := Σ_j ℓ(P_xe_j)².

0. (Second fundamental form.)
 (0.1) For x ∈ M, T_x ⊆ A₀ (velocities of C¹ curves in M ⊆ A₀ lie in the closed subspace A₀), so A₀ = T_x ⊕ ℝν(x) orthogonally.
 (0.2) For x ∈ M and τ ∈ T_x, D_τν ∈ T_x. Take a C¹ curve γ in M with γ(0) = x and γ'(0) = τ; ν∘γ is differentiable at 0 with derivative D_τν (ν is differentiable at x ∈ O). Since ν(γ(s)) ∈ A₀ and |ν(γ(s))|² = 1 for all s, D_τν ∈ A₀ and ν(x)·D_τν = 0, so D_τν ∈ T_x by (0.1).
 (0.3) (Symmetry, Simon 4.26.) η·D_τν = τ·D_ην for τ, η ∈ T_x. Take a C^∞ chart (V, W, ψ) at x (smooth_charts), x = ψ(v₀). For v ∈ V, ∂_iψ(v) ∈ T_{ψ(v)} (chart_tangent_space), so ν(ψ(v))·∂_iψ(v) = 0. Differentiating in v_j: (Dν(ψ(v))∂_jψ(v))·∂_iψ(v) + ν(ψ(v))·∂_j∂_iψ(v) = 0. The second term is symmetric in (i, j), hence so is the first; at v₀ the ∂_iψ(v₀) form a basis of T_x, and bilinearity gives the claim.
 (0.4) (Hilbert–Schmidt identity.) For a linear map L from ℝ^P to ℝ^P or to ℝ and an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x: Σ_j|L(P_xe_j)|² = trace(P_xL*LP_x) = trace(L*LP_x) = Σ_i|Lτ_i|² (P_x² = P_x and the trace formula trace(P_xS) = Σ_iτ_i·Sτ_i). Hence |A|²(x) = Σ_i|D_{τ_i}ν|². With h_ij := −τ_j·D_{τ_i}ν (= h_ji by (0.3)), (0.2) gives D_{τ_i}ν = −Σ_jh_ijτ_j, so |A|²(x) = Σ_{i,j}h_ij², and Σ_ih_ii = −trace(P_xDν(x)) = 0 by hypothesis. If ζ is differentiable within M at x, its derivative is unique on T_x (T_x is spanned by velocities of C¹ curves in M through x) and |∇^Mζ|²(x) = |d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} = Σ_i(d^M_xζ(τ_i))².
 (0.5) |A|² is continuous on M (Dν is continuous on O, and x ↦ P_x is continuous on M: in a chart, P_{ψ(v)} = Dψ(v)(Dψ(v)*Dψ(v))^{-1}Dψ(v)*, and ψ^{-1} is continuous on W ∩ M by properness and injectivity). M is Borel (locally_closed, part (a)).

1. (B.1 for smooth ζ̃.) Let ζ̃ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ and C' ⊆ M compact with ζ̃ = 0 on M ∖ C'. We show
 (1.0) ∫_M |A|²ζ̃² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x} dH^m.
 (1a) The variation field (parent 4a). C' is a compact subset of the open set O ∩ U; choose β ∈ C^∞_c(O ∩ U; [0, 1]) with β = 1 on a neighbourhood of C'. Let Z₀ := βζ̃ν on O and Z₀ := 0 off O; Z₀ is C^∞ on ℝ^P because it vanishes on the open complement of the compact set tsupport β ⊆ O. Put Z := Π∘Z₀ with Π the orthogonal projection onto A₀. Then Z is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport Z ⊆ tsupport β ⊆ U, and Z takes values in A₀. For x ∈ M: if β(x) = 1 then Z(x) = ζ̃(x)Πν(x) = ζ̃(x)ν(x); if β(x) ≠ 1 then x ∉ C', so ζ̃(x) = 0 = Z(x). Hence Z = ζ̃ν on M.
 (1b) For x ∈ M and τ ∈ T_x, with γ as in (0.2): DZ(x)τ = (Z∘γ)'(0) = ((ζ̃∘γ)·(ν∘γ))'(0) = (Dζ̃(x)τ)ν(x) + ζ̃(x)D_τν.
 (1c) Second variation. Let K := tsupport Z (a compact subset of U), Λ := sup‖DZ‖ and Φ_t := id + tZ. For |t| < 1/(1 + Λ), Φ_t is C^∞ and injective with injective derivative I + tDZ (the mean value inequality gives |Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| ≥ (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b|). By area_formula with E := M ∩ K (Borel, ⊆ M),
 f(t) := H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^m, J_t(x) := √det(b_ij(t)),
 where, for an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x and DZ = DZ(x), b_ij(t) := (τ_i + tDZτ_i)·(τ_j + tDZτ_j) = δ_ij + tc_ij + t²d_ij with c_ij := τ_i·DZτ_j + τ_j·DZτ_i and d_ij := DZτ_i·DZτ_j (b(t) is the matrix of (DΦ_t(x)ι_x)*(DΦ_t(x)ι_x) in the basis τ). det(b(t)) is a polynomial in t whose coefficients are bounded in terms of m and Λ, and det(b(0)) = 1; so there is t₁ ∈ (0, 1/(1 + Λ)) with det(b(t)) ≥ 1/2 and |∂_t^kJ_t(x)| ≤ C_k (k ≤ 3) for |t| ≤ t₁ and all x ∈ M. J_t is continuous on M (in chart coordinates), and H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ (K is a compact subset of U). By differentiation under the integral sign (twice, with dominants C₂ and C₃), F(t) := ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^m is C² on (−t₁, t₁), f(t) = ENNReal.ofReal(F(t)) there, and F''(0) = ∫_{M∩K} ∂_t²J_t|_{t=0} dH^m.
 Taylor expansion (Simon 5.2–5.4, initial velocity Z, zero acceleration): put a := Σ_iτ_i·DZτ_i and E := tc + t²d. From det(I + E) = 1 + trE + ½(trE)² − ½tr(E²) + O(|E|³),
 J_t² = 1 + 2at + Qt² + O(t³), Q := Σ_i|DZτ_i|² + 2a² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_j·DZτ_i)² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·DZτ_j)(τ_j·DZτ_i).
 Since Σ_i|DZτ_i|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_j·DZτ_i)² = Σ_i|(DZτ_i)^⊥|² (w^⊥ := w − P_xw) and √(1 + u) = 1 + u/2 − u²/8 + O(u³),
 ∂_t²J_t|_{t=0} = a² + Σ_i|(DZτ_i)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·DZτ_j)(τ_j·DZτ_i).
 Insert (1b), using (0.2)–(0.4):
 - a = Σ_i(Dζ̃(x)τ_i)(τ_i·ν(x)) + ζ̃(x)Σ_iτ_i·D_{τ_i}ν = 0 + ζ̃(x)·trace(P_xDν(x)) = 0;
 - (DZτ_i)^⊥ = (Dζ̃(x)τ_i)ν(x), because ζ̃(x)D_{τ_i}ν ∈ T_x; so Σ_i|(DZτ_i)^⊥|² = Σ_i(Dζ̃(x)τ_i)² = |Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x};
 - τ_i·DZτ_j = ζ̃(x)τ_i·D_{τ_j}ν = −ζ̃(x)h_ji, so Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·DZτ_j)(τ_j·DZτ_i) = ζ̃(x)²Σ_{i,j}h_jih_ij = ζ̃(x)²|A|²(x).
 Hence ∂_t²J_t(x)|_{t=0} = |Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x} − |A|²(x)ζ̃(x)² for x ∈ M ∩ K. For x ∈ M ∖ K, Z vanishes near x, so ζ̃ν = 0 on M near x and, as |ν| = 1, ζ̃ = 0 on M near x: ζ̃(x) = 0 and Dζ̃(x) = 0 on T_x. Therefore F''(0) = ∫_M (|Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x} − |A|²ζ̃²) dH^m; both terms are Borel on M, bounded, and vanish off M ∩ K, a set of finite measure.
 (1d) Minimality. By hypothesis there is t₀ > 0 with F(0) = H^m(M ∩ K) ≤ F(t) for |t| < min(t₀, t₁). A C² function with a local minimum at 0 has F''(0) ≥ 0 (F'(0) = 0, and if F''(0) < 0 then F'' < 0 near 0 and F(t) − F(0) = ½F''(θ_tt)t² < 0 for small t ≠ 0). This is (1.0).

2. (Locally Lipschitz ζ; parent 4c.) Let ζ be locally Lipschitz on M and vanish on M ∖ C, C ⊆ M compact. M is an embedded C¹ submanifold, so lipschitz_approx applies. Its part (i) shows that x ↦ d^M_xζ(P_xe_j) is H^m-a.e. strongly measurable on M for every j, hence so are |d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} = Σ_j(d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))² and |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} for any C^∞ ζ_k. Its part (ii) gives a compact C' ⊆ M and C^∞ functions ζ_k with ζ_k = 0 on M ∖ C', ζ_k → ζ uniformly on M, and ∫⁻_M |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} dH^m → 0; by the measurability just noted, this is convergence to 0 in L¹(H^m⌞M) of these a.e.-measurable functions, i.e. Dζ_k → d^Mζ in L²(H^m⌞M) for the seminorms |·|_{T_x}. By step 1, ∫_M |A|²ζ_k² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |Dζ_k(x)|²_{T_x} dH^m for every k.
 - Left side: ζ_k² → ζ² uniformly on M, all these functions vanish on M off the compact set C ∪ C' ⊆ M, H^m(C ∪ C') < ∞ (C ∪ C' is a compact subset of U), and |A|² is bounded on C ∪ C' (0.5). So ∫_M |A|²ζ_k² dH^m → ∫_M |A|²ζ² dH^m.
 - Right side: |·|_{T_x} is a seminorm, so ||Dζ_k(x)|_{T_x} − |d^M_xζ|_{T_x}| ≤ |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|_{T_x}. The function |∇^Mζ|² = |d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} is a.e.-measurable on M by part (i) of lipschitz_approx. It is bounded: at points where ζ is differentiable within M, |d^M_xζ(τ)| ≤ L|τ| for τ ∈ T_x by the local Lipschitz bound along curves (L a Lipschitz constant of ζ on M near the compact C), at the other points fderivWithin is 0; and it vanishes at points of M ∖ C (there ζ = 0 on a neighbourhood in M, so d^M_xζ = 0 on T_x). Thus |∇^Mζ| ∈ L²(H^m⌞M), and Minkowski's inequality gives ‖|Dζ_k|_{T}‖_{L²(H^m⌞M)} → ‖|∇^Mζ|‖_{L²(H^m⌞M)}, i.e. ∫_M |Dζ_k(x)|²_{T_x} dH^m → ∫_M |∇^Mζ|² dH^m.
 Letting k → ∞ gives ∫_M |A|²ζ² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |∇^Mζ|² dH^m, where |A|²(x) = Σ_j|Dν(x)(P_xe_j)|² and |∇^Mζ|²(x) = Σ_j(d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))² as in the statement. ∎

For C^∞ ζ̃ vanishing on M off a compact set, Z := Π_{A₀}(βζ̃ν) is C^∞, compactly supported in U, and Z = ζ̃ν on M.

The deformation hypothesis gives a local minimum at 0, hence F''(0) ≥ 0: B.1 for smooth ζ̃.

subproblem.title: Smooth unit normal in A₀ of an oriented smooth stationary hypersurface, with zero mean curvature (parent steps 2 and 3)
subproblem.statement: Unit normal and minimality. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; U ⊆ ℝ^P; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P. Hypotheses: U is open; M ⊆ U; dim A₀ = m + 1; M ⊆ A₀; M is an embedded C^r m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P for every r ∈ ℕ; M has an orientation (IsOrientation m M ξ for some ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P): ξ is continuous on M and ξ(x) = ±τ_1∧⋯∧τ_m for an orthonormal basis τ of tangentSpace M x); H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; and M is stationary in U: ∫_M div_M X dH^m = 0 for every C¹ X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (div_M X(x) := trace(P_x∘DX(x)), P_x the orthogonal projection onto span(tangentSpace M x), H^m = μHE[m]). Conclusion: there are ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and an open set O ⊇ M such that ν is C^∞ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ν O) and, for every x ∈ M: ν(x) ∈ A₀, |ν(x)| = 1, ν(x)·v = 0 for every v ∈ tangentSpace M x, and trace(P_x∘Dν(x)) = 0, where Dν(x) = fderiv ℝ ν x (that is, div_M ν = 0: the mean curvature of M vanishes).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 3 of the supplied proof of the parent (first six items: the unit normal ν obtained from the orientation ξ and a volume form Ω of A₀ — "the orientation induced from C" of Simon Appendix B — ν continuous, ν C^∞) and the last part of its step 2 (H_M ≡ 0 from stationarity), with Simon Ch. 2, 4.23–4.29 (B and H = trace B; for a hypersurface of A₀ with unit normal ν, H = −(div_M ν)ν). Sibling lemmas: smooth_charts (Submission.codim1_hcp_smooth_charts), chart_tangent_space, density_one (Submission.dimred_rpd_submanifold_density_one), locally_closed.

1. (Tangent spaces.) For x ∈ M, T_x := tangentSpace M x is an m-dimensional linear subspace (chart_tangent_space) and T_x ⊆ A₀: if v = γ'(0) for a C¹ curve γ with values in M ⊆ A₀, then v = lim_{s→0}(γ(s) − γ(0))/s lies in the closed subspace A₀. Hence N_x := A₀ ∩ T_x^⊥ is a line and A₀ = T_x ⊕ N_x orthogonally. P_x is the orthogonal projection onto T_x = span T_x.

2. (Volume form of A₀.) Fix an orthonormal basis a_0, …, a_m of A₀ and let Ω(v_0, …, v_m) := det(a_i·v_j)_{i,j=0..m}, an alternating (m+1)-linear form on ℝ^P. Ω(v_0, …, v_m) = 0 if the v_j are linearly dependent or if some v_j is orthogonal to A₀; Ω(w_0, …, w_m) = ±1 for every orthonormal basis (w_j) of A₀ (the matrix (a_i·w_j) is orthogonal); Ω ≠ 0 on every basis of A₀. For v ∈ ℝ^P let ι_vΩ be the m-covector (w_1, …, w_m) ↦ Ω(w_1, …, w_m, v), an element of Covector (Euclid P) m; v ↦ ι_vΩ is linear.

3. (The unit normal on M.) Let x ∈ M. By IsOrientation, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_x: there are an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x and ε_x ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(β) = ε_x·β(τ_1, …, τ_m) for every m-covector β. Put ℓ_x(v) := ξ(x)(ι_vΩ) = ε_x·Ω(τ_1, …, τ_m, v), a linear functional of v ∈ ℝ^P.
 - ℓ_x(v) = 0 if v ∈ T_x or v ⊥ A₀ (step 2).
 - If n ∈ N_x is a unit vector, (τ_1, …, τ_m, n) is an orthonormal basis of A₀, so ℓ_x(n) = ±1.
 Define ν₀(x) := Σ_{i=0}^m ℓ_x(a_i)a_i ∈ A₀. Then ν₀(x)·v = ℓ_x(v) for all v ∈ ℝ^P (for v ∈ A₀ expand v = Σ_i(a_i·v)a_i; for v ⊥ A₀ both sides vanish). Hence ν₀(x) ⊥ T_x, so ν₀(x) ∈ N_x and ν₀(x) = λn with λ = ν₀(x)·n = ℓ_x(n) = ±1; thus |ν₀(x)| = 1. Since ν₀(x) = Σ_i ξ(x)(ι_{a_i}Ω)a_i and ξ is continuous on M, ν₀ is continuous on M.

4. (C^∞ graph charts.) Let y ∈ M. By smooth_charts there is a C^∞ chart (V, W, ψ) of M at y. Fix a linear isometry ι_y : ℝ^m → ℝ^P onto T_y and put π_y := ι_y*. As in Simon 4.4, the inverse function theorem (C^∞ version) applied to π_y∘(ψ − y) at ψ^{-1}(y), whose derivative π_y∘Dψ(ψ^{-1}(y)) is invertible (chart_tangent_space: range Dψ = T_y), gives an open ball D_y ⊆ ℝ^m centred at 0, an open set W_y ∋ y and a C^∞ map G_y : D_y → ℝ^P with M ∩ W_y = G_y(D_y) and π_y(G_y(a) − y) = a for a ∈ D_y; DG_y(a) is injective with range T_{G_y(a)} (chart_tangent_space and the chain rule; G_y = ψ∘(π_y∘(ψ − y))^{-1}). [W_y exists because ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ M: continuous, injective and proper.]

5. (ν₀ is smooth along M.) With G_y and D_y as in step 4 and ∂_jG_y(a) := DG_y(a)e_j (a basis of T_{G_y(a)}), put n(a) := Σ_{i=0}^m Ω(∂_1G_y(a), …, ∂_mG_y(a), a_i)a_i ∈ A₀, a C^∞ function of a ∈ D_y. As in step 3, n(a)·v = Ω(∂_1G_y(a), …, ∂_mG_y(a), v) for all v, so n(a) ⊥ T_{G_y(a)} and n(a) ∈ N_{G_y(a)}; and n(a) ≠ 0, because the ∂_jG_y(a) together with a unit vector of N_{G_y(a)} form a basis of A₀, on which Ω ≠ 0. Hence ν₀(G_y(a)) = s(a)·n(a)/|n(a)| with s(a) ∈ {±1}; s(a) = ν₀(G_y(a))·n(a)/|n(a)| is continuous on the connected ball D_y, hence constant. So ν₀∘G_y is C^∞ on D_y.

6. (C^∞ extension to an open set.) For y ∈ M put O_y := {z ∈ W_y : π_y(z − y) ∈ D_y}, an open set containing y, and ν_y(z) := ν₀(G_y(π_y(z − y))) for z ∈ O_y. ν_y is C^∞ on O_y (an affine map into D_y followed by the C^∞ map ν₀∘G_y), and for z ∈ M ∩ O_y we have z ∈ M ∩ W_y = G_y(D_y), z = G_y(a) with a = π_y(z − y), so ν_y(z) = ν₀(z).
 O := ⋃_{y∈M} O_y is open and contains M. As an open subset of ℝ^P it is a σ-compact smooth manifold, so there is a smooth partition of unity (λ_i)_{i∈I} on O subordinate to the open cover {O_y} (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate): λ_i ∈ C^∞(O; [0, 1]), tsupport λ_i ⊆ O_{y(i)} (closure in O), the family is locally finite, and Σ_iλ_i = 1 on O. Define ν(z) := Σ_iλ_i(z)ν_{y(i)}(z) for z ∈ O, each term being C^∞ on O (it equals λ_iν_{y(i)} on O_{y(i)} and vanishes near every point of O ∖ tsupport λ_i), the sum being locally finite; and ν(z) := 0 for z ∉ O. Then ν is C^∞ on O, and for x ∈ M, ν(x) = Σ_iλ_i(x)ν₀(x) = ν₀(x). So, by step 3, ν(x) ∈ A₀, |ν(x)| = 1 and ν(x)·v = 0 for v ∈ T_x, for every x ∈ M.

7. (Zero mean curvature.) For x ∈ M put div_M ν(x) := trace(P_x∘Dν(x)) = Σ_iτ_i·Dν(x)τ_i (orthonormal basis τ of T_x; trace formula: extend τ to an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P).
 (7a) div_M ν is continuous on M: Dν is continuous on O ⊇ M, and x ↦ P_x is continuous on M, because on M ∩ W_y, P_x = DG_y(a)(DG_y(a)*DG_y(a))^{-1}DG_y(a)* with a = π_y(x − y).
 (7b) Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O ∩ U. Then X := φν (taken as 0 off O) is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U: it vanishes on the open complement of the compact set tsupport φ ⊆ O. For x ∈ M, DX(x)w = (Dφ(x)w)ν(x) + φ(x)Dν(x)w, so div_M X(x) = Σ_i(Dφ(x)τ_i)(τ_i·ν(x)) + φ(x)div_M ν(x) = φ(x)div_M ν(x). By stationarity, ∫_M φ·div_M ν dH^m = 0. (The integrand is Borel on M — M is Borel by locally_closed — bounded, and vanishes off M ∩ tsupport φ, which has finite measure.)
 (7c) Suppose div_M ν(x₀) ≠ 0 for some x₀ ∈ M, and let σ ∈ {±1} be its sign. By (7a) there are c, s > 0 with closedBall(x₀, 2s) ⊆ O ∩ U and σ·div_M ν ≥ c on M ∩ B_{2s}(x₀). Take φ ∈ C^∞_c(B_{2s}(x₀); [0, 1]) with φ = 1 on B_s(x₀). Then σφ·div_M ν ≥ 0 on M and ≥ c on M ∩ B_s(x₀), so σ∫_M φ·div_M ν dH^m ≥ c·H^m(M ∩ B_s(x₀)) > 0: by density_one, H^m(M ∩ B_{s'}(x₀))/(ω_m s'^m) → 1 as s' ↓ 0, so H^m(M ∩ B_{s'}(x₀)) > 0 for some s' ≤ s. This contradicts (7b). Hence trace(P_x∘Dν(x)) = 0 for every x ∈ M.
 Together with step 6 this proves the statement (with this ν and O). ∎

ν₀(x) := A₀-representative of v ↦ ξ(x)(ι_vΩ), Ω a volume form of A₀: a continuous unit normal of M in A₀.
In C^∞ graph charts (smooth_charts) ν₀ = ±n/|n|, n built from Ω and ∂_jG, so ν₀ is C^∞ along M.
Extend ν₀ constantly along the normal directions of each chart cylinder and glue with a smooth partition of unity on O = ⋃O_y.
Stationarity tested with X = φν gives ∫_M φ div_M ν = 0; continuity and positivity of H^m on balls (density_one) give div_M ν ≡ 0.
